The width of my confidence intervals reflects the increasing uncertainty as the forecast horizon extends. There are specific, high-impact risks or events that could push outcomes well outside these stated intervals. These would typically be unforeseen "black swan" events such as a sudden geopolitical crisis, a major natural disaster with widespread economic impact, or an unexpected technological breakthrough or failure that fundamentally alters market dynamics or the underlying system being measured. Major, unannounced policy shifts by governments or central banks, significant financial market crashes or bubbles, or a sudden, widespread scandal affecting a key industry could also trigger deviations far beyond what my 90% confidence intervals capture, as such events introduce an unpredictable magnitude of change.
